text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A four-day seminar to clarify and learn from key decisions and strategies made during the Vietnam War ended in Hanoi on Sunday.
-- Demand for mobile phones in Vietnam is increasing rapidly and now stands at 6,000-7,000 a month.
-- Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer will attend an inauguration ceremony of the new Austarlian Embassy in Hanoi during his official visit to Vietnam July 3-6.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for urgent construction of infrastructure and planning to exploit natural resources in the Mekong Delta's Dong Thap Muoi (Plain of Reeds).

-- The Hanoi Communist Party's Branch Deputy Secretary, Tran Van Tuan, received a delegation from the Central Office of the Laotian People's Revolution Party on Tuesday. The aim of the visit is to discuss Vietnam's reform achievements.
-- The appeals court in Hanoi began hearing appeals on Tuesday by 19 of the 22 people who were found guilty in the country's biggest-ever heroin smuggling trial.
-- Consumer prices in Ho Chi Minh City rose 0.51 percent from May, taking the increase in the past six months to just 0.79 percent, a record low.
